case_notes.content: Carl called back confirming Jumpstart can be his transportation and he'll be there Friday.

Intake Screening: Carl Allen
Date: 10/28/2026 | Staff: Daisy | Type: Phone consultation
Outcome: Offered the open orientation slot this Friday (10/30, 3 PM), with a Monday start. That depends on him confirming a ride. He was calling Jumpstart to check and said he’d call back within about 5 minutes.

Housing

Living in housing provided through Jumpstart.
Says he can stay there up to 2 years.

Documents

Birth certificate: Yes
Social Security card: Yes
State ID: Yes
Driver’s license: Yes, valid

Transportation

He thinks Jumpstart will drive him to and from the program but isn’t sure. He’s confirming with them.
Told him Turn90 doesn’t provide transportation.
Gave him the Spartanburg Dial-a-Ride number as a backup: 864-560-4118. Rides need to be booked by about 10 AM the day before.

Availability

No conflicts with 9–3, Monday through Friday, apart from occasional doctor’s appointments. He confirmed the hours work.

Health / Substance Use

Prescribed blood pressure medication in the last 5 years. He currently has access to it.
No history of major alcohol abuse.
History of long-term meth use, which led to homelessness at one point. Clean for over 2 years without a formal treatment program.
Told him about drug testing at orientation and weekly after that, including marijuana. He said, “I’m clean.”
Legally and physically able to work, with no health limitations.
No immediate or emergency needs.

Justice Involvement

Age at first arrest: about 13
Total arrests: about 7–8 
Convictions: about 7–8
Most recent release: October 1 (2026), from prison, after about 5 years
Most recent conviction included drug trafficking: No
Included firearm possession: No
Biological parents’ criminal record: Both parents are deceased.
On parole with about 5 more months left (around March 2027). He’s in compliance.
Turn90 is not a condition of his parole.
Pending charges: None

Education / Employment

Highest education: GED
Work history: construction (possibly “remodeling construction”) and cable assembly.
Longest job: possibly about a year (unclear).
His last job was cable assembly, which he did while incarcerated. It sounded like a prison industries (PIE) job.
Current certifications: IPC certification and J-Standard certification (electronics assembly and soldering).
Child support: None

Program Info Given

8 weeks, Monday through Friday, 9–3. $450 a week. Job placement with a partner employer at the end.
Mornings are a CBT-focused group class. The rest of the day is job training: forklift certification and SkillCat online trade courses (HVAC, etc.).
Weekly one-on-one with a case manager.

Next Steps

Wait for Carl’s call back confirming his ride from Jumpstart.
Confirm the Friday orientation time with him. You told him 3 PM but said you’d double check.
If his ride is confirmed: he attends orientation on Friday 10/30 and starts Monday 11/2.
